alex_dev: Quick q — planning release for SDK v2. For /v1/embeddings: what input types do we accept (string, list of strings, nested), truncation behavior, batch limits, and output dims? Need to write tests.

sophia_ml: Supports plain string and array[string]. Don't accept nested arrays (no batching of batches) — pass batches as top-level array.

sophia_ml: Truncation: tokenizer-based to model context window. For redwood-emb-large we cap at 8192 tokens; redwood-emb-small cap 4096. We silently truncate tokens at the tokenizer boundary (no 400 error), but we add a warning in response metadata when truncation happened.

alex_dev: Where is the warning surfaced? field name?

sophia_ml: Response includes meta.warnings array (string entries). Example:
```
{
  "data": [ { "embedding": [0.001, -0.02, ...], "index": 0 } ],
  "model": "redwood-emb-large-v1",
  "meta": { "warnings": ["input truncated to 8192 tokens"] }
}
```

alex_dev: Nice. What's the output vector shape for large vs small?

sophia_ml: large -> 1536 dims, small -> 768 dims. We guarantee fixed dim per model. Response returns list aligned with input order.

oliver_sre: Batch limits/rate: any per-request item limit? SDK currently sends 2048 inputs in one call in stress tests.

sophia_ml: Per-request item limit is 1024 for embeddings. If you send more we return 400 with message "batch size exceeds limit". Recommend chunking; Redwood SDK auto-chunks to 512 by default for safety.

infra-bot: docs updated: https://redwood.ai/docs/api/embeddings (edited) :doc:

jamie_pm: Backwards compat question — if we change model dims in a future model, how will we surface that to customers?

sophia_ml: Model dims are kept per-model. We add model profiles to model catalog and emit a new field 'model_version' and deprecate older models with 90 days notice. Also evals and perf profile published.

alex_dev: For unit tests, should I assert vector length or parse from response.model? what's recommended?

sophia_ml: Parse expected dim from the model name in response.model or from meta.model_profile.dim. But simplest: assert vector length equals len(response.data[0].embedding). We do both in SDK: we check against model catalog and fall back to response vector length.

alex_dev: Great. I'll update SDK to chunk to 512, pass through meta.warnings and surface them as warnings.warn() in python. Any concerns from SRE?

oliver_sre: Make sure chunking is retry-friendly and preserves order — include index in payload so we can reassemble. Also watch memory when auto-chunking.

sophia_ml: We include 'index' in each data item; server guarantees preserved ordering based on that index.

alex_dev: Perfect. I'll open PR referencing this thread. :tada:

infra-bot: PR linked: https://github.com/redwood/clients/pull/842

jamie_pm: TY everyone.
